segments.text: Verse 3
He neither begets nor is He begotten,
Allah declares Himself free of having offspring or being born. He has no child and was not born of a parent, as He says:
He neither begets nor is He begotten,
This truth prevents us from imagining the Lord in the way we imagine created beings with family lineages.
It is reported that the idolaters said to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him,
Name the lineage of your Lord for us.
Surah Al-Ikhlas was then revealed. Some scholars graded the core of this report hasan, or acceptable.

The reports differ over who asked: some identify idolaters and others People of the Book. The point here is to understand the error revealed by the form of the question. It is as though they wanted to place the Creator within the genealogies of created beings. The revelation introducing Him rejects that comparison, rather than supplying the kind of lineage they requested.

This differs from the question that arises in the heart of someone seeking guidance: Who is my Lord, and how can I know and worship Him? People ask about their own origins and may be deeply concerned to know their father, mother, and ancestry. Indeed, it is reported that ‘Abdullah ibn Hudhafah asked the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who his father was.
If this concerns a person, he has even more reason not to overlook knowing his Creator. But seeking to know Him is one thing; assuming that Allah has a lineage like a human being is another.
Allah says:
When My slaves ask you concerning Me, I am indeed near[1].
His servant seeks to know his Lord and draw near to Him, and revelation answers with guidance, rather than encouraging him to measure Allah against himself.
Surah Al-Ikhlas is a preserved answer for the person who asks, and awakens the question in someone whom worldly concerns have distracted from it.

Attributing offspring to Allah is not a trivial claim to repeat without understanding its implications. In a hadith qudsi—divine speech reported by the Prophet—Allah explains that the son of Adam denies Him by saying He will not bring him back as He created him, then says:

As for his abusing Me, it is his saying that Allah has begotten children, while I am the One, the Self-Sufficient Master Whom all creatures need, I beget not, nor was I begotten, and there is none like unto Me.
Just as denying the resurrection is a denial of His truth, claiming that He has offspring disparages Him and contradicts what He has made known about Himself.
The Quran depicts the enormity of this claim in these words:
at which the heavens are about to be torn apart, the earth split asunder, and the mountains tumble down.
Then the next verse states the reason:
because they have ascribed to the Most Compassionate a son.

If this is how its effect on the heavens, earth, and mountains is portrayed, how can a believer pass over it heedless of his Lord’s right? Reverence for Allah requires declaring Him free of this claim and recognizing its falsehood, rather than becoming so accustomed to it that its gravity fades from the heart.
Denying that Allah has a lineage also corrects the way we turn to Him.
Someone might try to gain access to a person in authority through his father or son, or think a relative could compel him to respond. Allah’s pleasure, however, is not sought on this human model.
He has no father or son through whom pressure could be brought upon Him or something He disapproves of obtained. His servant calls on Him and repents to Him directly.

This brings relief and mercy to the sinner: he does not need to expose what has been concealed about him to another human being who would grant him forgiveness, nor take his confession to an idol or to someone he imagines has authority over Allah.
Moses said,
My Lord, I have wronged myself, so forgive me,
and Allah tells us:
Then He forgave him
He recognized his wrong and brought his need to his Lord. The door of repentance is not in the keeping of an imagined relative of Allah; it is with Allah Himself.

publisherNotes.text: [1] Allah’s nearness means that one does not need to raise his voice or to ask for intercession in order that his prayers be answered.
